title: row25; allocator design defect, trigger written by us
live_proof: inspection with a line number in the 3.22.0 tree: memsys5 writes Mem5Link{next,prev} into the body of a freed block at src/mem5.c:143 (MEM5LINK), keeping only CTRL_FREE out of band in aCtrl[]. Design-inherent and never patched, so it is live in the pin and in every other release
object: a caller's block returned to the memsys5 pool, whose bytes become freelist metadata
lifetime_ender: sqlite3_free returns the block to the pool and a neighbour free makes memsys5 link and coalesce, writing in-band metadata through the caller's storage
fidelity: PROPOSED FOR WITHDRAWAL as the corpus's premise demonstrator, not as a case whose trigger misses. Constructed demonstrator over the real allocator: the trigger is ours, not an upstream input -- it allocates two adjacent blocks, holds a pointer to the first, frees both so memsys5 coalesces, then reads back through the held pointer. That makes it the one case here whose consumer is the case itself, which is also why its probe site is in the case source and not in sqlite3.c. It is the same construction the arms already ship as their positive control, controls/control_uaf_mem5.c, with one extra free so the in-band overwrite is observable, so the two measure one event on every run. The premise it states -- to ASan the whole pool is one allocation, so this is invisible at the layer below -- is worth keeping in the corpus as a demonstrator; it is not a found defect, and counting it adds one to the denominator and one to Sublet's numerator for a reading the control already provides

note: WITHDRAWAL PROPOSED 2026-10-16, reason: this is the corpus's premise demonstrator and the same construction as the arms' own positive control, not a second defect. controls/control_uaf_mem5.c, which its own header labels CONTROL, not a case, allocates with sqlite3_malloc, frees, and reads back through the dead pointer; this case does that and adds a neighbour free, so memsys5's coalesce writes Mem5Link through the dead block's body and the stale read returns freelist indices instead of the caller's bytes. Both therefore measure one event on every Sublet run, and counting this one as a case adds 1 to the denominator and 1 to Sublet's numerator for a reading the control already provides. The control's header states what tools/arms.json requires of it -- memsys5 stock completes, memsys5 on its Sublet port faults -- and that is line for line what this case measured on 2026-10-16, so the case's result is the control's declared expected behaviour. Three further facts argue for withdrawal rather than for a rewritten trigger. (1) upstream_fix is mem5-design: there is no SQLite defect here and no fix to point at, by design and in every release, so there is no upstream input that could replace our trigger. (2) consumer is run_case -- the dangling read is in our own code, which is why the probe site is in the case source and not in sqlite3.c; every other case in this corpus has an upstream consumer function. (3) The host-ASan oracle on record was taken without memsys5, so it does not witness the phenomenon the case names. The measurements stay in PROVENANCE.md because the demonstration is worth having: virtual-malloc returns rc=0 after reading 4294967295 out of a block that held 2779054080, which is this corpus's premise stated as a number, and Sublet rejects that same read with cause 25. Keep the directory and the source as a demonstrator; exclude it from the counted corpus
fault_sites_why: The stale access is the case's own READ through the dangling pointer after memsys5 linked metadata into the freed block (consumer run_case; PROVENANCE.md). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs.
